title: Effective-dated security identity: one alias interval (schema_version 1)
description: One row of the collector's security master. Producer: collectors/security_master.py::build_master (STUB: no S3 product, no unit, no consumer yet). Resolution (collectors/security_master.py::resolve) returns exactly one security_id for an alias on a date or refuses: unresolved and ambiguous are explicit, never a fallback to the current ticker. alpha-engine-config-I12568 (audit DATA-02).

master_version.description: The build this row belongs to. A master is published whole per version and never edited in place, so each version is a vintage of the identity table.

security_id.description: Permanent security id, minted once from the security's first listing (ticker, date, CIK, share class); never re-used. collectors/security_master.py::mint_security_id.

alias_type.description: What alias_value is. A ticker is a provider/display alias; CUSIP/FIGI/exchange are a later slice (alpha-engine-config-I12568).

alias_value.description: Ticker in the fleet's class-suffix form (BRK-B), or the decimal CIK.

share_class.description: Share class when the issuer lists more than one (BRK-A / BRK-B are distinct securities sharing a CIK).

effective_from.description: First NYSE session date the alias means this security (inclusive).

effective_to.description: First session date it no longer does (exclusive); null while in effect. Intervals of different securities never overlap for one alias.

source.description: The event source the interval was built from.

as_of.description: Point-in-time: the trading day this record describes (ISO date, NYSE calendar). data_collection_plan_260914.md §2 objective 4; contracts/pit.py.

available_at.description: Point-in-time: the UTC instant the producer could first have known this record (RFC 3339, Z suffix). Never before the as_of day begins, never after the publishing run's manifest `finished`. contracts/pit.py.

x-pit.rule: Each build publishes the whole table as a new master_version and never edits an earlier one, so a replay reads the newest version available by its decision. available_at is the build's data_pit stamp: when the identity was established, not when the alias took effect.
